To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heat transfer coefficient increases with the increase in the inlet velocity, the increase in the nanoparticle volume fraction and the decrease in the nanoparticle diameter.

the heat transfer coefficient is enhanced by increasing the inlet velocity, increasing the particle volume fraction, and decreasing the nanoparticle size, however, the pressure drop and pumping power are also increased by these parameters.

the heat transfer enhancement is achieved by increasing the particle volume fraction, decreasing the particle diameter and/or increasing the Reynolds number, however, the increment of heat transfer coefficient is accompanied by an increase in pressure drop and pumping power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of Reynolds number, particle volume fraction, and nanoparticle diameter on forced convective thermal performance of a nanofluid flow inside an axisymmetric microchannel.
forced convective heat and mass transfer in microchannels.

the effects of the particle volume fraction, Reynolds number, nanoparticle diameter, and viscous dissipation on heat transfer and performance evaluation criterion of nanofluid flow inside an axisymmetric microchannel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the heat transfer coefficient of the nanofluid in microchannels is more than the pure water, and the heat transfer augmentation of the nanofluidd is more than the base fluid, and the heat exchangers with the microchannels can be more compact and the pumping power can be reduced.
the heat transfer coefficient is not a function of Reynolds number and particle volume fraction, but it is a function of nanoparticles diameter and viscous dissipation.
, in order to achieve the best possible heat transfer coefficient, the Reynolds number and the particle volume fraction must be increased, but the nanoparticle diameter should be reduced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heat transfer augmentation of the nanofluid flow is considerable in the entrance region of the microchannel, and the effect of the particle size on heat transfer is negligible.
the heat transfer augmentation is not always in favor of the system.
, in microchannels the viscous dissipations effect is significant and the thermal behavior of a fluid is totally different from that in a macro scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the system is affected by both heat transfer augmentation and pressure losses.
the heat transfer coefficient and the performance evaluation criterion can be improved by increasing the inlet Reynolds number.
, the performance evaluation criterion is a valuable parameter for microchannel heat exchangers.
